name: # Golden Crust Bakery
brief:
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

## Mission
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.

## Mission
# Golden Crust Bakery — Marketing Website

## What this is
A marketing website for a neighbourhood bakery called Golden Crust. The site is
public, read-mostly, and exists to get a hungry visitor to walk in or place an
order. It must be fast on a phone, work without JavaScript for the core content,
and be trivially editable by the owner.

## Audience
- Local residents deciding where to buy bread and pastries today.
- People ordering a celebration cake or a catering box ahead of time.
- Tourists searching "bakery near me" on a phone.

## Required pages / sections
1. **Home** — hero with today's fresh-bake highlights, opening-hours badge that
   shows Open/Closed computed from the current time and the hours table, and a
   short story block.
2. **Menu** — grouped products (Breads, Pastries, Cakes, Drinks). Each item has a
   name, short description, price, and allergen tags (gluten, dairy, nuts, egg,
   vegan). Filter by dietary tag and by category, plus a text search box.
3. **Hours & Location** — a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures
   list, an embedded static map image, and a "Get directions" link.
4. **Order form** — a celebration-cake / catering enquiry form: name, phone,
   email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes. Must validate the
   pickup date is at least 48 hours in the future, require either phone or email,
   and show a clear confirmation with an order reference.
5. **Contact** — phone, email, address, social links, and a short FAQ.

## Functional requirements
- Opening-hours logic must be a single source of truth reused by the Home badge
  and the Hours page (compute Open/Closed from the same table).
- The menu filter must combine category, dietary tag, and free-text query with
  AND semantics, and show a friendly empty state when nothing matches.
- The order form must reject a missing contact method, a pickup date under 48
  hours away, and a quantity below 1; on success it generates a human-readable
  order reference (e.g. GC-2026-0007) and echoes the full order back.
- Prices are shown in GBP with two decimals; totals for quantity > 1 are
  computed.
- All form validation errors are field-level and accessible (associated with the
  input, announced to screen readers).

## Non-functional requirements
- Responsive from 320px to 1440px; mobile-first.
- Core content (menu, hours, contact) readable with JS disabled.
- Semantic HTML landmarks, one h1 per page, alt text on every image.
- Colour contrast at least WCAG AA.
- No third-party trackers.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Online payment / card processing.
- User accounts or login.
- A real database or CMS backend — content is static data in the app.
- Multi-language support.

Hours & Location page must show a weekly table of opening hours, a holiday-closures list, an embedded static map image, and a Get directions link.

Order form must collect name, phone, email, pickup date, product, quantity, and free-text notes, and on success generate a human-readable order reference of the form GC-YYYY-NNNN and echo the full order back with a clear confirmation.

Order form validation must reject a missing contact method (neither phone nor email provided), a pickup date under 48 hours in the future, and a quantity below 1, with phone or email requiring at least one but not both.
Opening-hours Open/Closed logic must be a single source of truth function reused by both the Home badge and the Hours page so both derive from the same hours table.
Totals for quantity greater than 1 must be computed from unit price and quantity and displayed in GBP with two decimals alongside the order echo.
All form validation errors must be field-level, associated with their input, and announced to screen readers.

edgeCases: A moment exactly 48 hours before the pickup date must be rejected or accepted consistently per the under-48-hours rule, pinned by a test using a fixed clock.
A pickup date exactly at opening time versus exactly one minute past closing must map to the same open/closed result as the hours table defines.
Midnight-wrapping opening hours (close time earlier than open time) must compute correctly rather than reporting Closed all night.
Today falling on a listed holiday closure must force the badge to Closed even when the weekly table says open.
A day with no rows in the hours table must render as Closed rather than crashing.
An empty menu query plus no category plus no tag must return all items grouped by their categories.
A search string matching zero items, or a category/tag combination matching zero items, must show the friendly empty state instead of a blank list.
Search must be case-insensitive and match on name and description so 'SOUR' finds 'Sourdough'.
A quantity of exactly 1 must not show a computed total line, while quantity 2 must show unit price times 2 in GBP with two decimals.
An order where phone is blank and email is filled, and the inverse, must both pass the contact requirement; both blank must fail.
Duplicate submissions of an identical order arriving close together must each get a distinct order reference.
A generated order reference must follow GC-YYYY-NNNN with the year taken from the submission time and a zero-padded sequence.
A free-text notes field containing only whitespace must be treated as empty.
Rendering with JavaScript disabled must still expose the full menu, weekly hours, and contact details as static markup.
A pickup date string that is not a parseable date must be rejected as a field-level date error, not silently coerced.
Viewport widths at exactly 320px and exactly 1440px must show all core content without horizontal scrolling.
errorHandling: Missing or unparseable pickup date must surface a field-level error tied to the date input and keep the rest of the entered order intact.
Pickup date under 48 hours ahead must surface a field-level error explaining the 48-hour minimum.
Quantity below 1 or non-numeric must surface a field-level error on the quantity input.
When neither phone nor email is present, surface a field-level contact error; when only one is present, accept and no error.
Successful submission must show a confirmation containing the generated GC-YYYY-NNNN reference and the echoed order fields.

Because no backend or database exists, submission failure may only arise client-side (validation or reference generation); any thrown error must be caught and shown as a non-destructive user-facing message rather than a blank screen.
A menu filter combination yielding nothing must degrade to the friendly empty state message, never an error or crash.
An image missing alt text or a page missing exactly one h1 must be treated as a build/test failure rather than shipping.

dataFlow: Static content data (menu items, hours table, holiday closures, contact details, FAQ) is authored in-app as typed constants with no backend or CMS.
Page render reads the static data and produces semantic HTML with landmarks, one h1, and alt text on every image.
Home render passes the shared hours table and current time into computeOpenStatus to produce the Open/Closed badge label.
Hours page render passes the same hours table and current time into the same computeOpenStatus function so both pages agree.
Menu render groups items by category, then applies filterMenuItems combining category, allergen, and case-insensitive query with AND semantics.
A filter result of zero items diverts rendering to the friendly empty state instead of the item list.
Order form input is collected, whitespace-only notes normalized to empty, and passed to validateOrder which returns per-field errors.
On validation failure, field-level errors are associated with their inputs and announced to screen readers and the entered order is preserved.
On validation success, generateOrderReference(now) creates GC-YYYY-NNNN, computeOrderTotal derives the total when quantity exceeds 1, and submitOrder resolves an OrderConfirmation.
The confirmation is rendered as a clear success view echoing reference, all order fields, and the GBP two-decimal total.
Any client-side throw during submission is caught and rendered as a non-destructive user-facing message with the form still intact.
